nodes.label: Brand Design Rule
nodes.rationale: Mandates loading docs/pocket/rule/creative-brief.md before any UI/UX planning or development because that file is the project's design system authority; no UI decision should be made without consulting it.

nodes.label: DragonDB Visual SQL
nodes.rationale: Product direction: Visual SQL learning + query building, PostgreSQL first. Expand capability only when each new SQL concept can remain understandable in the visual model.

nodes.label: SQL Mode
nodes.rationale: SQL mode remains the direct text-editing environment; visual mode helps construct and understand.

nodes.label: Core Learning Loop
nodes.rationale: Build visually -> see generated SQL -> run query -> see result -> change something -> understand what changed. A successful roadmap should make this loop deeper over time without turning the product into a visual representation of every SQL grammar rule.

nodes.label: Query Model / Intermediate Representation
nodes.rationale: Visual cards should mutate a query model / IR, not concatenate SQL strings directly; this keeps logic reusable if the visual chrome changes later.

nodes.label: PostgreSQL
nodes.rationale: Primary database: PostgreSQL first; Phase 0 is PostgreSQL only.

nodes.label: Phase 0: Thin Slice / Core Execution Loop
nodes.rationale: First risk is not JOINs/subqueries/CTEs but whether the interaction (block -> SQL -> result) feels useful at all; a narrow but polished loop gives much better signal than broad SQL support with weak interaction design.
nodes.norm_label: phase 0: thin slice / core execution loop

nodes.label: Phase 1: Make Understand What It Generates Real
nodes.rationale: The brand promise's second half (understand what it generates) is weak if generated SQL is hidden behind an occasional modal; users should connect visual action, generated SQL fragment, and resulting rows.
nodes.norm_label: phase 1: make understand what it generates real

nodes.label: Phase 2: Everyday Single-Table Queries
nodes.rationale: A query builder becomes genuinely useful when users can answer normal filtering questions without leaving the visual model; maximize usefulness before introducing relational complexity.

nodes.label: Phase 3: Relational SQL / JOIN
nodes.rationale: JOIN is where SQL becomes meaningfully relational and where beginner confusion rises sharply, so the visual UI can provide substantial value beyond syntax completion; JOIN is the first major complexity jump and its own product milestone.

nodes.label: Phase 4: Summaries and Analytics
nodes.rationale: Many users query databases to answer questions (how many, how much, average, highest, lowest, per customer/month/category); this is where DragonDB becomes useful for analysts rather than only SQL beginners inspecting records.

nodes.label: Phase 5: Power-User Bridge
nodes.rationale: Visual programming has a complexity cliff; provide a controlled path from visual construction into more expressive SQL so the product becomes a bridge instead of a beginner-only dead end.

nodes.label: Phase 6: Visual SQL Learning Bridge
nodes.rationale: Deliberately later because round-trip conversion is substantially harder than one-way visual -> SQL generation; round-trip capabilities become more valuable after the visual query model itself has stabilized.

nodes.label: SUMMARIZE Experience
nodes.rationale: Present aggregation as a user-intent block (SUMMARIZE: group rows by / calculate) compiled to SELECT ... GROUP BY underneath, so beginners do not reason directly about GROUP BY grammar.

nodes.label: Custom SQL Escape Hatch
nodes.rationale: For concepts expensive or confusing to represent visually, allow an advanced escape hatch rather than expanding the node grammar indefinitely; exact design should be validated before implementation.

nodes.label: Collapsible Generated SQL Inspector
nodes.rationale: Optional read-only inspector on the right of the visual workspace: closed by default, opened from View generated SQL, ~300-350px initial width, resizable, read-only, copy action, updates immediately when visual state changes.

nodes.label: SQL Change Feedback
nodes.rationale: When a meaningful visual action changes the generated SQL, optionally highlight or emphasize the affected fragment; can start simple without a full semantic diff engine.

nodes.label: Schema-Aware Assistance
nodes.rationale: Show columns from both tables, use foreign-key metadata to suggest likely relationships, disambiguate duplicate column names, handle table aliases internally; suggestions assist, not prevent, manual configuration.

nodes.label: Beginner-Facing JOIN UI
nodes.rationale: Prefer intent-oriented choices: Combine this table with another table, Match (users.id = orders.user_id), Rows to keep (only matching rows vs keep every users row).

nodes.label: Learning Annotations
nodes.rationale: Help users understand relationships such as contains -> LIKE '%value%', Only matching rows -> INNER JOIN, Keep every row from the first table -> LEFT JOIN.

nodes.label: Explain Existing SQL
nodes.rationale: Given a supported SQL query, show a readable structural explanation (e.g. SELECT name FROM users WHERE active = true -> Read from users, Return name, Keep rows where active equals true).

nodes.label: SQL to Visual Reconstruction
nodes.rationale: For a supported subset of SQL, reconstruct the visual representation; only attempted when the mapping is predictable enough to avoid surprising users.

nodes.label: Product North Star
nodes.rationale: Success is a user moving from 'I don't remember SQL syntax' to 'I know what this SQL is doing'. DragonDB does not win by keeping users dependent on blocks; it wins when visual interaction gives enough confidence and understanding that SQL stops feeling inaccessible.

nodes.label: Brand Line: Build SQL Visually, Understand What It Generates
nodes.rationale: DragonDB should not position Visual mode as a way to avoid SQL forever; the goal is to help people become capable with SQL by manipulating familiar concepts visually, seeing the generated SQL, running it, and observing the result.
nodes.norm_label: brand line: build sql visually, understand what it generates

nodes.label: Product Principles
nodes.rationale: Five principles: (1) visual concepts represent user intent, not a strict 1:1 SQL keyword mapping; (2) visual and SQL are two representations of one query; (3) prefer progressive complexity; (4) do not chase complete SQL coverage, use escape hatches; (5) preserve a reusable query model / IR.

nodes.label: Later / Research Track
nodes.rationale: Potential areas that should not block the main roadmap: nested Boolean expression groups, more JOIN types, window functions, advanced CTE support, PostgreSQL-specific expressions, schema relationship visualization, freeform canvas, reusable query fragments, saved visual templates, query explanation/learning hints, multi-database dialect support, AI-assisted query construction. Each justified by real user demand.

nodes.label: Explicit Non-Goals
nodes.rationale: Visual mode is not: a visual representation of the entire PostgreSQL grammar, an n8n clone, a replacement for the SQL editor, a system that hides SQL forever, an AI text-to-SQL wrapper, or a full ETL/workflow automation product.

nodes.label: DragonDB
nodes.rationale: Multi-database client with a visual SQL builder — so beginners can query without writing syntax. Audience: data/business analysts and data scientists early in SQL fluency; grounding over intimidation. After using DragonDB the user should feel 'tidak takut SQL lagi'.

nodes.label: Visual SQL Builder
nodes.rationale: Visual builder sits on defined SQL, not a new dynamic language — keeps the product calm and precise.

nodes.label: Brand Persona
nodes.rationale: Professional, friendly, and precise — a calm, native-feeling desktop tool on every platform, making databases approachable without dumbing them down. Emotional goal: 'tidak takut SQL lagi' (no longer afraid of SQL).

nodes.label: Neutral-Friendly Register (Tone of Voice)
nodes.rationale: Neutral-friendly: clear, warm, plain language; sentence case; lead with verbs; no slang, no emoji in product UI, sparing exclamation. Friendly wins on tone and emotional goal; precise + professional win on structure.

nodes.label: OKLCH Color System
nodes.rationale: oklch() is native CSS, so every value is used verbatim as a custom property — no conversion, no recomputation. Hex codes are reference only.

nodes.label: CTA Fill primary-600 Rule
nodes.rationale: CTA fill uses primary-600, not 500 — white on 500 fails AA (3.33:1); white on 600 passes (4.81:1). Gate 3 auto-adjust.

nodes.label: Typography Scale (1.20 Minor Third)
nodes.rationale: Base 16px, ratio 1.20 (Minor Third — data-dense desktop). The ratio follows the platform class, not the font, so it is unchanged from the SF Pro era.

nodes.label: Inter (Bundled Body Font)
nodes.rationale: Bundled with the app, not loaded from a CDN — a Tauri artifact must work offline. Bundling buys identical metrics on all three platforms and reliable font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums, which the result grid depends on and the Windows system font does not deliver dependably.

nodes.label: JetBrains Mono (Bundled Mono Font)
nodes.rationale: Bundled because SwiftUI got a mono face free from the system but CSS needs it declared; required by the SQL editor and the Generated SQL inspector.

nodes.label: Tabular Numerals (font-variant-numeric)
nodes.rationale: Result-grid numeric cells set font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums so digits align across rows; Windows system font does not deliver this dependably.

nodes.label: Focus Ring Rule
nodes.rationale: A webview has no system focus ring, so every ring is drawn explicitly: outline: 2px solid var(--primary-600); outline-offset: 2px. The 2px offset gap renders the page background, so governing contrast is ring-against-background (4.81:1 on white, 4.43:1 on neutral-100 panel, both ≥3:1). Do not implement as an inset box-shadow — on a primary button that puts primary-600 against primary-600 and the ring disappears.

nodes.label: Tauri v2 (Cross-Platform Desktop)
nodes.rationale: Cross-platform desktop (web frontend + Rust core) on macOS, Windows, Linux; platform class for scale purposes: data-dense desktop app. WebKitGTK on Linux is the least consistent of the three engines — any new component gets checked there before it is called done.

nodes.label: SwiftUI App (Legacy, Frozen)
nodes.rationale: Retained because the Swift app stays alive on bugfix-only maintenance during the Tauri transition. Do not build new roadmap phases against it. SwiftUI mapping retained as legacy; system focus rings available there.

nodes.label: CSS Custom Properties Tokens
nodes.rationale: Emit every value as CSS custom properties on :root; use oklch() values verbatim rather than converting to hex at call sites. Name tokens --primary-600, --neutral-900, --error-solid matching the brief's shade names so a review can diff brief against stylesheet by name.

nodes.label: Dark Mode (Known Gap)
nodes.rationale: Dark mode is not defined. Multi-theme support is an explicit later extension of brand-design; until refined in, the app ships light-only on all three platforms. Inherited for free from system appearance in SwiftUI and not free in a webview.

nodes.label: Cross-Platform Amendment (Revision)
nodes.rationale: Scope of revision: platform, font, focus rings, implementation notes. The OKLCH palette and every contrast ratio are unchanged — oklch() is native CSS and transfers verbatim. Preview regenerated 2026-08-10; prior confirmation 2026-08-09 (original, macOS/SwiftUI).

nodes.label: Generated SQL Inspector
nodes.rationale: Roadmap Phase 1 feature; the SQL editor and the Generated SQL inspector need a mono face (JetBrains Mono).

nodes.author: brainstorm session (pocket-grinding)
nodes.rationale: Pulls a thin end-to-end path (real I/O, connect, Run SELECT) into SP-2 so the author can manually verify 'it works like the spec' before SP-3/SP-4b polish.

nodes.label: Cross-Platform Design (parent SP map)
nodes.source_location: Related Areas; IPC Contract Delta intro; Implementation Notes

nodes.label: dragondb-swift reference app
nodes.rationale: Full reference implementation (ConnectionService, PostgresNIO, Citadel SSH, Keychain, SwiftData models) to mirror in Rust with recorded exceptions.

nodes.label: IPC Contract Delta
nodes.rationale: Authoritative extension of parent §4 IPC for SP-2 grinding scope: profile CRUD + connectProfile/disconnect plus structured IpcError transport; parent §4 alone was incomplete.

nodes.label: ConnectionProfileDto
nodes.rationale: Persisted profile fields never include password or key material; secrets travel only via ProfileSecretsInput to keyring.

nodes.label: Rust I/O modules (postgres/ssh/secrets/storage)
nodes.rationale: Rust = thin I/O, no runtime mocks; real IPC implementation replacing the Tauri stub; established crates, not hand-rolled crypto/SSH/SQL.

nodes.label: tokio-postgres
nodes.rationale: Async Postgres client chosen over sqlx (pool/macros heavier than single-conn thin I/O).

nodes.label: russh
nodes.rationale: Async SSH + direct-tcpip; rejected ssh2 for C/libssh2 friction.

nodes.label: keyring 4.x
nodes.rationale: Secrets only in OS credential store (default v1 feature); parent design's keyring 3.6 snippet is stale and must not be copied.

nodes.label: rusqlite (bundled)
nodes.rationale: Local app DB with full schema for five Swift models; rejected sqlx-sqlite for sync CRUD; no password column in sqlite.

nodes.label: Rough connection UI
nodes.rationale: Rough create/edit/save/delete profile, Save-then-Connect, Disconnect, switch-with-confirm now; polished shell deferred to SP-4b.

nodes.label: Canvas Run control
nodes.source_location: Scope In-Scope; Stories — Canvas Run (SELECT); Implementation Notes
nodes.rationale: Net-new Run control on canvas toolbar/chrome; SELECT-only execute path for SP-2 exit; status-only OK / N rows / X ms, no results grid.

nodes.label: Visual-query IR (src/core)
nodes.rationale: Must stay DOM/Tauri/store-free; IR stays TypeScript; Run executes generateSQL(doc).exec.

nodes.label: Save-then-Connect rule
nodes.rationale: connectProfile requires a saved profile; Connect without Save is rejected so secrets are written to keyring before any connection attempt.

nodes.label: SSH tunnel lifecycle
nodes.rationale: Tunnel before DB, DB via 127.0.0.1:ephemeral, teardown on disconnect/failure so no orphan tunnel remains; SSH tunnel mandatory for SSH exit.

nodes.label: One-shot reconnect
nodes.source_location: Scope In-Scope; Stories — Dead SSH socket scenario
nodes.rationale: Dead socket while Connected triggers tunnel+DB rebuild once then retry once, opaque inside Rust runQuery/metadata ops; after explicit disconnect, no silent reconnect.

nodes.label: SELECT-only Run gate
nodes.source_location: Scope In-Scope; Stories — Rule 4; Implementation Notes
nodes.rationale: Run CREATE gated in the UI Run handler (no runQuery, no history, clear human message) without changing core canRun(CREATE) card-building fidelity; Run CREATE deferred vs Swift.

nodes.label: QueryHistory write side effect
nodes.rationale: Silent history insert inside Rust runQuery after execute (success or fail), not a separate UI call; gated CREATE never calls runQuery.

nodes.label: Canvas full interaction lock
nodes.source_location: Scope In-Scope; Stories — Full lock scenario
nodes.rationale: Disable add/edit/remove cards, statement picker and Run until Connect — not merely canRun eligibility; after disconnect, cards preserved as read-only snapshot with SQL preview readable.

nodes.label: ConnectionId lifecycle
nodes.rationale: connectProfile issues connectionId (opaque; may equal profileId or session token — planning picks one stable scheme); disconnect invalidates it and UI must not reuse the old id.

nodes.label: SSL mode mapping
nodes.source_location: IPC Contract Delta — SSL mode table
nodes.rationale: Six SslMode values with Swift parity; allow/prefer collapse to disable; verify-ca/verify-full hidden/disabled in UI when sshEnabled.

nodes.label: Option A thin session
nodes.rationale: Chosen: thin session in App + expand DragonIpc, no full SP-3 store layer; rejected Option B (full stores delays proof) and Option C (debug harness fails no-mock + canvas Run).

nodes.label: No app-data migration
nodes.source_location: Stories — No app-data migration; Rollback Plan
nodes.rationale: Explicit non-migration decision: no SwiftData importer; Mac upgraders' profiles/queries/history/tabs do not transfer; release notes must state this.

nodes.label: Structured IpcError transport
nodes.rationale: Failing methods reject with structured IpcError (kind + message) serialized across Tauri invoke; UI must never parse free-form strings; unknown mapped to 'unknown'.

nodes.label: Modular Zustand Stores (Option A)
nodes.rationale: Chosen option: separate stores for session, schema, tabs, library, history + pure util modules + IPC/schema expansion. Rejected Option B (monolith store: harder selective subscribe, large PRs, fights Zustand rationale) and Option C (logic-heavy Rust: violates thin I/O, pure utils become IPC round-trips). Best fit for per-tab results, SP-4b selectors, and Swift composition.

nodes.label: ConnectionStringParser
nodes.rationale: Swift port: parse + validate + sslmode + build() round-trip + error taxonomy. Hand-rolled rather than a new npm library because it is a fidelity port of an existing Swift utility, not greenfield crypto/auth.

nodes.label: CSVExporter (from raw, RFC4180 escape)
nodes.rationale: CSV must be generated from raw (not compact) results; quote only when needed (comma/newline/quote), empty/nil → bare empty field, not "". SP-4b must use raw for CSV/export accuracy.

nodes.label: QueryEditability (full rule table)
nodes.rationale: Full rule table beyond JOIN-only: CTE, UNION/INTERSECT/EXCEPT, GROUP BY, DISTINCT, window, aggregates, multi-FROM, JOIN → isEditable=false with Swift-parity reasons; sourceTable short-circuit yields editable; simple single-table SELECT extracts tableName/schema.

nodes.label: RowOperationsService / RowOperationError
nodes.rationale: Mirror Swift error kinds: noPrimaryKey, noTableSelected, noRowsSelected, metadataFetchFailed, updateFailed, deleteFailed; support .null edit values where Swift does. DB unchanged on validation errors.

nodes.label: TabState DTO (full Swift field set)
nodes.rationale: Migrate + hydrate ALL Swift TabState fields including cachedResultsData blob. Two persist modes mirroring TabService/TabManager: metadata/text sync without re-encoding blob, and results sync (encode/write blob + column names write-on-success). Compact is recomputed from raw on hydrate, not a separate persist field.

nodes.label: Swift Parity (ports vs dragondb-swift)
nodes.rationale: Pure utils are Swift ports, not new npm SQL/CSV frameworks. Hand-rolling connection-string parse / CSV escape / splitter is justified as fidelity ports of existing Swift utilities, not greenfield crypto/auth. Amend folded all BLOCKING + IMPORTANT findings from the Swift parity review into Scope/checklists/Stories/AC.

nodes.label: SP-4b UI Clusters (ten clusters)
nodes.rationale: SP-4b is UI-heavy (ten clusters); without stores every UI session re-ports Swift logic or invents half-stores inside components — the exact failure SP-4a was forbidden to create. SP-3 must be SP-4b-ready foundations with zero regression on the verified learning loop.

nodes.label: rusqlite id-only stubs (saved_queries/query_folders/tab_states)
nodes.rationale: saved_queries / query_folders / tab_states are id-only stubs; query_history write-on-run exists with no delete/clear helpers. SP-3 migrates stubs to Swift-parity columns via additive sqlite migrations (forward-compatible, no destructive down-migration).

nodes.label: History Field Mapping (SP-2 superset)
nodes.rationale: Maps SP-2/Tauri columns to Swift QueryHistory fields (id, profile_id→connectionId as profileId, sql→queryText, success→isSuccess, duration_ms→executionTime, created_at→executionDate) keeping SP-2 extras error_message and row_count; databaseName optional. listHistory newest-first, profileId optional → global list; clearHistory always per-profile, never global wipe.

nodes.label: Late-result / generation-guard async safety
nodes.rationale: In-flight Run → ignore late results after disconnect/switch; late Run after tab switch lands on the executing tab; schema store generation guard ignores late listTables rows after disconnect/switch; pending-deleted tab ids ignore further writes. Intentional stricter-than-Swift (no soft cancel required) — OK for store correctness.

nodes.label: Dual raw+compact per-tab model
nodes.rationale: Intentional Tauri model: Swift browse often caches compacted-only; editor Run does not compact. Full tab blob persist size cost accepted for Swift parity. SP-4b must use raw for CSV/export accuracy.

nodes.label: Clear-at-start on new Run (documented divergence)
nodes.rationale: Intentional SP-3/orchestration choice: clear in-memory per-tab result at new Run start. Swift editor often keeps prior rows until completion — documented divergence, do not claim editor 1:1 on this point.

nodes.label: Zustand dependency decision
nodes.rationale: Rejected Context-only (re-render/selector cost) and Jotai (atomic model less natural for session/tab modules); not a server-cache library. Lock exact current-major version in planning.

nodes.label: SP-4b Remaining UI — Swift Parity Prerequisite Ledger
nodes.norm_label: sp-4b remaining ui — swift parity prerequisite ledger

nodes.label: SEQUENCE Disposition
nodes.rationale: Remaining clusters are SEQUENCE, never silent-drop: required for full SP-4b complete but after first-slice. Every SEQUENCE row must stay on the done-bar.

nodes.label: DROP (dead) Disposition
nodes.rationale: DROP only when Swift view is unreachable from DragonDBApp/RootView with cited evidence; behaviors that still live elsewhere remain SHIP/SEQUENCE.

nodes.label: needs-decision Disposition
nodes.rationale: Code exists on both sides or behavior is ambiguous; product intent is not guessed — flagged for decision rather than silently dropped.

nodes.label: Canvas-Primary Editor Decision
nodes.rationale: A literal MainSplitView clone (saved-queries | SQL editor over results) would demote the visual canvas and fight SP-4a. Swift hosts the canvas as a mode inside QueryEditorView; Tauri already shipped the canvas as the primary editor. Swift behaviors must still land somewhere; the view tree must not be cloned.

nodes.label: Database Picker Gap
nodes.rationale: Largest functional gap vs Swift: Tauri session is one profile.database while Swift connects to server then picks a database; treating them as equivalent would silently drop the multi-database workflow.

nodes.label: SQL Editor Hatch
nodes.rationale: Shipping a Swift-like SQL-primary split would undo SP-4a; the SQL hatch should be a secondary surface (drawer/toggle) over the same results grid, bound to tabs.active.queryText.

nodes.label: History Relative Date Labels
nodes.rationale: formatRelativeDate uses Date.parse but rusqlite created_at is epoch-millis text (chrono_like_utc_now), so the UI echoes the raw number; tests pass because they feed ISO strings.

nodes.label: Missing Rust / IPC (listDatabases, create/delete database, cancel)
nodes.norm_label: missing rust / ipc (listdatabases, create/delete database, cancel)

nodes.label: ResizableSplitView (dead)
nodes.rationale: Defined but never instantiated; live splits are SwiftUI NavigationSplitView / VSplitView / HSplitView.

nodes.label: ConnectionsListView (dead)
nodes.rationale: No caller outside its own file/preview; behaviors duplicated by dropdown + form.

nodes.label: ColumnRowView (dead)
nodes.rationale: Never instantiated; live table expander is TableColumnRowView inside TablesListView.swift.

nodes.label: Badge (dead)
nodes.rationale: Only used by unreachable ColumnRowView; PK/FK icons in the table expander remain SEQUENCE.

nodes.label: SP-4b First Slice — App Shell + Read-Only Results
nodes.author: brainstorm session (pocket-grinding)
nodes.norm_label: sp-4b first slice — app shell + read-only results

nodes.label: This-Session Status Gate
nodes.rationale: status.kind is the only gate for the grid: idle shows empty copy even if hydrated compact is non-null; running shows Loading; ok shows compact table or 'No rows found'; error shows 'Query Failed'. rowCount/durationMs are never rendered.

nodes.label: Start Over Resets Canvas + Results
nodes.rationale: Start over resets the document and clears the results pane together, ignores late in-flight IPC, and does not delete history DB rows — intentional divergence from Swift QueryState.

nodes.label: SELECT-only Run Rule
nodes.rationale: Run is disabled unless connected, statementKind === 'select', and canRun.isRunnable. CREATE/UPDATE/DELETE cannot fire runQuery — disable in toolbar instead of changing core canRun(CREATE) semantics.

nodes.label: Design Decision: Option B
nodes.rationale: Library split chosen so pane sizes are independent of grid content and nested groups remain available for the SEQUENCE sidebar. Option A (hand-rolled CSS split) rejected because content can blow the ratio and nested split would be rewritten; Option C (data-grid library) rejected because filter/sort/virtualization are out of scope.

nodes.label: Anti-Glitch Generation Wiring
nodes.rationale: Grid is never filled from the canvas onRunQuery promise; Start over bumps store generation AND canvas runGeneration/runInFlight before next paint so late IPC applies are no-ops and there is no Loading-to-grid flicker.

nodes.label: Layer Boundaries (core/ stays pure)
nodes.rationale: Work may touch src/ui/**, App.tsx, App.css and a thin tabs-store hydrate guard, but must NOT touch src/core/ (except reading statementKind/canRun/generateSQL), src-tauri/**, or IPC contract expansion. Architecture validation: PASS (2026-08-14).

nodes.label: Accepted Tradeoffs
nodes.rationale: New small UI dependency vs layout glitches; unbounded SELECT row count accepted (Swift editor parity); SP-4a always-on SQL (S10) temporarily reverted; divider not persisted across relaunch.

nodes.label: SEQUENCE Clusters (deferred SP-4b)
nodes.rationale: Sidebar, tab bar, SQL editor, history UI, row edit/JSON/filter/sort/pagination, connection polish, database picker, static pages remain SEQUENCE in the parity ledger — not silent drops.

nodes.label: canvasEpoch
nodes.rationale: Canvas is one React tree keyed by canvasEpoch (profile switch), not per tab; keeps visual docs in-session only.

nodes.label: QueryDocument (per-tab visual)
nodes.rationale: Per-tab QueryDocument lives in UI/session memory keyed by tab id, synced on mutate; deliberately NOT added as a TabStateDto column this slice (no sqlite IR migration).

nodes.label: B' saved-query result cache
nodes.rationale: B' is an in-memory map savedQueryId -> compact+ok written on applyRunSuccess while the tab's savedQueryId matches; read on saved-query click; dropped on profile switch. It is the canvas-side analogue of the Swift SQL-editor result cache.

nodes.label: Welcome gating rule
nodes.rationale: Welcome shows iff 0 profiles and form hidden, so the empty app is not a blank form; ConnectionPanel must be able to hide the form when profile count is 0.

nodes.label: Queries column
nodes.rationale: Saved queries get their own resizable column left of the canvas (not inside ConnectionPanel) so named queries can be picked without a SQL editor.

nodes.label: Connection string mode
nodes.rationale: Lets users paste a postgres:// URL instead of retyping fields; parsed on Save via connection-string.ts; edit is read-only with Copy.

nodes.label: Native app menu (Help/Shortcuts/Settings)
nodes.rationale: Native menu via Tauri (not a hand-rolled fake menu bar); Help shows Support URL + shortcut list; accelerators actually bound.

nodes.label: Option A - compose columns in App
nodes.rationale: Chosen: compose columns in App; Queries width via react-resizable-panels; per-tab visual documents in session memory; native Tauri menu. Connection stays always visible this slice.
nodes.norm_label: option a - compose columns in app

nodes.label: Option B - AppShell wrapper (rejected)
nodes.rationale: Rejected: same pixels, extra file; rejected as ceremony.

nodes.label: Option C - collapsible connection sidebar (deferred)
nodes.rationale: Swift-real (NavigationSplitView); deferred to next grinding and recorded on the parity ledger, not dropped. Parent 12.1 forbids silent-drop.

App.tsx owns mock IPC wiring and mounts the canvas full-window; component-local QueryDocument with an explicit revision counter; no src/stores; no Run button; CREATE in scope, UPDATE/DELETE are Coming soon states.

nodes.label: Tauri v2 + React 19 + TypeScript + Bun stack
nodes.rationale: Tauri v2, React 19, TypeScript, Bun, Vitest (+ jsdom + Testing Library), Biome, CSS custom properties from the creative brief, @fontsource/inter + @fontsource/jetbrains-mono for local fonts.
nodes.norm_label: tauri v2 + react 19 + typescript + bun stack

nodes.label: QueryDocument revision counter
nodes.rationale: QueryDocument mutators update the instance in place. Every canvas mutation must bump a React revision (setRevision(r => r + 1) or equivalent) after the mutator returns so DOM/preview re-render without remounting a new QueryDocument instance.

nodes.label: Committed-FROM invalidation
nodes.rationale: Expose QueryDocument.committedFromTable getter; canvas mutations go through one wrapper that compares committed FROM before/after and calls onCommittedFromChange on any change (commit, popover select, delete FROM, start over). Typing via setFromTableText must not notify.

nodes.label: src/core purity boundary
nodes.rationale: src/core must stay free of DOM / Tauri / ui / stores / ipc, enforced by tsconfig.core + Biome + tests/architecture/core-boundary.test.ts. Reuse core TableReference in helpers and callbacks; convert to IPC TableRef only at the listColumns call site.

nodes.label: DragonIpc IPC contract
nodes.rationale: src/ipc/contract.ts defines ConnectionId, TableRef, ColumnInfo, QueryResult, IpcError, DragonIpc (listTables/listColumns/runQuery), FIXTURE_CONNECTION_ID; imports ExecutableSQL type from ../core.

nodes.label: Mock DragonIpc fixtures
nodes.rationale: createMockDragonIpc(mode) with MockMode happy/emptyTables/emptyColumns/columnsError; fixture tables users (public) and analytics.events; runQuery present but unused by UI.

nodes.label: TableRef to TableReference helpers
nodes.rationale: src/ipc/table-ref.ts: tableRefToCore, coreToTableRef, formatTableDisplayName (bare name when schema null or public), sameTable.

nodes.label: VisualQueryCopy strings
nodes.rationale: Ports VisualQueryCopy.swift verbatim plus extras: emptyCanvasTitle 'Build a query visually', noMatchesTitle 'No matches', sqlPreviewEmpty '—', columnsLoadError 'Could not load columns. You can still type a name.'

nodes.label: VisualQueryAccessibility test ids
nodes.rationale: data-testid constants matching Swift VisualQueryAccessibility strings; allInteractiveIdentifiers must be unique and include runQuery/modeToggle/confirm ids even if unused in SP-4a UI.

nodes.label: OKLCH design tokens (tokens.css)
nodes.rationale: Light-only; CSS variables on :root from creative brief OKLCH values (--primary-100..900, --neutral-100..900, semantic tint/solid/text), --radius: 4px, .focus-ring with outline 2px solid var(--primary-600).

nodes.label: Inter + JetBrains Mono local fonts
nodes.rationale: src/ui/fonts.css imports @fontsource/inter and @fontsource/jetbrains-mono weights; bundled locally, no CDN (test asserts no fonts.googleapis/jsdelivr/unpkg).

nodes.label: SchemaFieldPopover
nodes.rationale: Ports SchemaFieldPopover.swift: search filter case-insensitive, empty state message (needsFromMessage ?? errorMessage), list data-testids; used by FROM and column fields.

nodes.label: StatementPicker
nodes.rationale: Renders VisualQueryCopy.statementMenuItems(); Coming soon badge on update/delete; data-testid statementMenu, statementMenuItem(kind).

nodes.label: VisualQueryToolbar (Start over)
nodes.rationale: ONLY Start over control — no Run, no View generated SQL link (live preview is separate); test asserts no button named 'run query'.

nodes.label: GeneratedSQLPreview
nodes.rationale: Always-on read-only SQL preview (no Done dismiss) using generateSQL(doc)?.display ?? '—'; Copy button uses navigator.clipboard.writeText, errors swallowed (no toast in SP-4a); mono font via --font-mono.

nodes.label: ClauseCard + field editors
nodes.rationale: SELECT/FROM/WHERE/ORDER BY/LIMIT cards against QueryDocument mutators; popovers wired via SchemaFieldPopover; FROM display uses formatTableDisplayName; column popovers pass needsFromMessage when FROM not committed; do not import TableRef into UI modules.

nodes.label: StatementRootCard (CREATE / Coming soon)
nodes.rationale: CREATE editable in SP-4a (table name + column list with fresh CreateColumn[] values); UPDATE/DELETE show Coming soon chrome only; type labels via VisualQueryCopy.createColumnTypeTitle.

nodes.label: VisualQueryCanvas component
nodes.rationale: Assembles clause chain, status strips and pickers; owns one QueryDocument for the lifetime of the mount (uncontrolled by default); required mutate wrapper compares committed FROM before/after, bumps revision, fires onDocumentChange/onCommittedFromChange; no Run / create-confirm sheet.

nodes.label: App wiring + stale-safe metadata loads
nodes.rationale: Module-level DEFAULT_IPC = createMockDragonIpc('happy') not recreated during render; mounts canvas full-window; listTables maps via tableRefToCore; onCommittedFromChange triggers generation-guarded listColumns; optional ipc prop for tests; UI never calls runQuery.

nodes.label: Column-load generation guard
nodes.rationale: Increment a monotonic generation for every committed-FROM change, including null, before clearing state; apply resolve/reject only while mounted and when the captured generation is still current; increment again on unmount; stale rejections do nothing.

nodes.label: No Run button / no runQuery from UI
nodes.rationale: Do not call runQuery from UI; do not add Run chrome. Validation help uses a status strip (canRun messages as-is). Execution deferred to SP-4b.
nodes.norm_label: no run button / no runquery from ui

nodes.label: Scaffold purge gate
nodes.rationale: Zero greet/demo leftovers is a hard exit — includes src/, index.html, public/, and Rust greet; enforced by tests/ui/scaffold-purge.test.ts; index.html title DragonDB with non-scaffold favicon.

nodes.label: TDD red-green workflow
nodes.rationale: Every task is red-green: write failing test first, verify FAIL, implement minimally, verify PASS, commit with explicit pathspecs; full TDD for Tasks 6-10; revisioned test harness required for controlled fields.

nodes.label: Explicit pathspec git hygiene
nodes.rationale: Before each commit, git status must show only that task's files; stage with explicit pathspecs only, never git add -A; stop and ask if the worktree has unrelated dirty files.

nodes.label: Manual verify sign-off log
nodes.rationale: Manual verify on macOS + Linux after Task 10 (checklist in spec 11.2), not automated in CI; sign-off artifact docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-10-sp4a-manual-verify-log.md required (Task 11); every required OS row must be PASS before SP-4a exit.

nodes.label: Deferred SP-4b / SP-3 / SP-2 work
nodes.rationale: Idiomatic React regroup of mirrored Swift modules (spec 9 tech debt), brief-pattern rewrite of canRun help strings, Run button / create-confirm execute / three-pane shell (SP-4b), real IPC (SP-3), Rust I/O (SP-2), WebKitGTK CI job — documented, do not implement in this plan.

nodes.label: DragonDB
nodes.rationale: Cross-platform (Windows/macOS/Linux) fork of O'Saasy, a macOS-only SwiftUI PostgreSQL client; its audience is disproportionately not on macOS. New non-fork repo rfxlamia/dragondb built on Tauri v2.

nodes.label: Tauri v2
nodes.rationale: Decision D1: TypeScript frontend with thin Rust I/O core; ~15MB bundle vs Electron's ~150MB, appropriate for a DB client (TablePlus ~50MB). IR stays in TS so Rust remains a dumb I/O layer.

nodes.label: Electron (rejected alternative)
nodes.rationale: Rejected: consistent Chromium rendering is a genuine advantage for an interaction-heavy visual builder, but ~150MB bundle and heavy RAM are poor fits for a DB client.

nodes.label: Visual SQL Builder
nodes.rationale: Product north star from ROADMAP.md: move a user from 'I don't remember SQL syntax' to 'I know what this SQL is doing'. Roadmap Phases 2-6 are almost entirely new UI surface.

nodes.label: Visual Query IR (src/core)
nodes.rationale: Pure IR in TypeScript - no DOM, no Tauri, no stores. Single-sourced: Rust never sees the query model, it receives finished SQL plus bound parameters. Files: query-document.ts, query-clause.ts, sql-generator.ts, validation.ts, canvas-presentation.ts.

nodes.label: Dual SQL output (D5)
nodes.rationale: Decision D5: generateSQL returns GeneratedSQL { display: literals inlined for the SQL inspector, exec: $1/$2 + params for execution }. Brand line requires human-readable SQL; placeholders would defeat the learning purpose. The one intentional behavior change in the SP-1 port.

nodes.label: Repository layout (D8/D9)
nodes.rationale: Decision D8: new non-fork repo rfxlamia/dragondb (GitHub hides forks from search; 0 stars means nothing to lose). Decision D9: existing repo renamed dragon-db -> dragondb-swift to avoid one-hyphen confusion in SP-0 commands. Tap is its own repo (rfxlamia/homebrew-dragondb).

nodes.label: Homebrew tap + curl installer (D4)
nodes.rationale: Decision D4: distribution via own Homebrew tap + curl installer adapted from termul. Cask postflight strips com.apple.quarantine so plain 'brew install --cask' has no Gatekeeper prompt; browser DMG downloads still hit Gatekeeper, so docs steer macOS users to brew/curl.

nodes.label: termul (prior art)
nodes.rationale: Tauri app by the same author with a working cask, curl installer, bats suite (388 lines), and release workflow - proven prior art for SP-5 distribution. Tap repo is source of truth (commit 5ccbf0e).

nodes.label: SP-0 Repo bootstrap
nodes.rationale: Create rfxlamia/dragondb, scaffold Tauri v2, carry over creative brief + .claude/ enforcement + this spec, port LICENSE and attribution. Low risk, no dependencies.

nodes.label: SP-1 Visual query IR to TypeScript
nodes.rationale: 585 LOC port of 5 Swift files (VisualQueryDocument, VisualSQLGenerator, VisualQueryValidation, VisualQueryClause, VisualQueryCanvasPresentation) to core/*.ts. High risk gate. Definition of done: five translated Swift test suites green under Vitest; transliteration guarded by tests, not redesign.
nodes.norm_label: sp-1 visual query ir to typescript

nodes.label: SP-2 Rust I/O
nodes.rationale: Rust I/O: tokio-postgres, SSH tunnel, keyring (per-OS cargo features), rusqlite (replaces SwiftData). ~2,500 LOC. No dependencies.

nodes.label: SP-3 Stores + real IPC
nodes.rationale: App state stores and real IPC implementing the §4 DragonIpc contract. ~5,000 LOC. Depends on SP-1, SP-2.

nodes.label: SP-4a First UI slice (visual canvas)
nodes.rationale: ~1,220 LOC: seven VisualQuery card components + VisualQueryCanvasView container + VisualQueryCopy. Runs against real core/ and mocked DragonIpc. Highest risk, sequenced second; answers whether block-card interaction survives the move to web UI. No store layer, no real IPC.

nodes.label: SP-4b Remaining UI (ten clusters)
nodes.rationale: ~7,926 LOC across ten clusters enumerated in §12.1 (app shell, connection, sidebar/saved queries, results grid, table browser, query editor, history, tab bar, DB management, static pages), each needing its own spec. Container, not a task; builds on SP-4a, swaps mocked DragonIpc for SP-3's real one.

nodes.label: SP-5 Distribution
nodes.rationale: Cask, installer, CI matrix (~1,100 LOC). Low risk - proven prior art (termul). Deferred last because the cost is scheduling, not risk.

nodes.label: SP-6 Swift freeze rule and parity gate
nodes.rationale: dragondb-swift accepts bug fixes only; no roadmap phase may be implemented in Swift; repository archived on GitHub once Tauri ships and passes the §13.1 parity gate. Separate repos make the rule largely self-enforcing.
nodes.norm_label: sp-6 swift freeze rule and parity gate

nodes.label: Module boundary rule (core purity)
nodes.rationale: src/core may not import from ui/, stores/, ipc/, or @tauri-apps/* and may not touch a DOM global. Three enforcement mechanisms: tsconfig.core.json lib without DOM, import-restricting lint rule, architecture test as regression backup. Roadmap Principle 5 ('visual cards mutate a query model, not SQL strings') upheld by CI.

nodes.label: IPC contract (DragonIpc)
nodes.rationale: src/ipc/contract.ts: listTables/listColumns/runQuery typed wrappers over invoke(); defined in parent doc because SP-4a mocks it and SP-3 implements it. ExecutableSQL imported from core, never redeclared. IpcError typed variants (connection/auth/syntax/permission/unknown).

nodes.label: ExecutableSQL
nodes.rationale: Generator's output type defined in core (src/core/sql-generator.ts) and imported by the IPC contract; a second definition in the IPC layer would be free to drift from the thing that actually produces the value.

nodes.label: Rust I/O layer (src-tauri)
nodes.rationale: tokio-postgres pool, SSH tunnel, keyring secrets, rusqlite storage. Rust never sees the query model - it receives finished SQL plus bound parameters. Error mapping from raw Postgres error to typed IpcError happens in Rust.

nodes.label: Keyring backend hazard
nodes.rationale: Keyring backend selection is a compile-time decision and failure is silent: without an OS-backend cargo feature, keyring falls back to an in-memory mock where set_password reports success and get_password always returns NoEntry. Replaces KeychainService; stores SSH private keys and DB passwords. Guarded by the §9 restart round-trip test.

nodes.label: Typed error chain
nodes.rationale: Existing Errors/ chain keeps its shape; mapping raw Postgres errors to domain types happens in Rust and crosses IPC as typed IpcError variants - never free-form strings, so the UI never parses messages. User-facing strings follow the brief's Copy Guidelines.

nodes.label: Testing strategy
nodes.rationale: core/ -> Vitest with five translated Swift suites as the port contract; Rust secrets -> process-restart integration test; Rust postgres/ssh -> container-backed Postgres; installer -> bats adapted from termul's 388-line suite; cross-platform -> WebKitGTK (Linux) checked explicitly for every new component (least consistent of the three engines).

nodes.label: Parity gate (SP-6, §13.1)
nodes.rationale: Archiving the Swift repo is blocked until every §12.1 cluster and §12.2 capability is shipped or explicitly dropped with a recorded reason. 'Proven stable on macOS' was replaced because nothing can fail it. Data migration decision must be made before archive, not at archive time.

nodes.label: Parity inventory (§12)
nodes.rationale: 52 files / 8,974 LOC in Views/, assigned to clusters in §12.1; §12.2 lists capabilities with no screen of their own (CSV export, SQLStatementSplitter, QueryTypeDetector, RowOperationsService, ConnectionStringParser, etc.). Arithmetic consistency is not feature coverage - ten of fifteen screens were unnamed in the first draft.

nodes.label: Data migration gap
nodes.rationale: No data migration path: connection profiles, saved queries, query history, tab state live in SwiftData in the old app and rusqlite in the new one. Either SP-2 gains an importer or release notes state data does not transfer - decided before SP-6, tracked in §13.1 checklist.

nodes.label: Creative brief / brand design
nodes.rationale: Amended 2026-08-10 (D7) before any UI work: platform, fonts (Inter + JetBrains Mono bundled locally), focus rings (outline + outline-offset), implementation notes; OKLCH palette unchanged. Fixes every visual token for SP-4a; Copy Guidelines govern user-facing strings; dark mode is an undefined later extension.

nodes.label: Roadmap (Phases 2-6)
nodes.rationale: docs/pocket/ROADMAP.md; phases 2-6 are new UI surface (multi-condition WHERE, JOIN builder, GROUP BY/HAVING, SQL inspector) and are paused during the 3-4 month port. Principle 5: visual cards mutate a query model, not SQL strings.

nodes.label: SwiftData-backed models
nodes.rationale: ConnectionProfile, SavedQuery, QueryHistory, QueryFolder, TabState - app data and app-flow concerns, not visual-query IR; belong to SP-2/SP-3 and move to rusqlite.

nodes.label: Block-Card Interaction Model
nodes.rationale: The highest remaining migration risk: whether the Swift block-card interaction model survives in a webview at creative-brief fidelity — the core question SP-4a answers.

nodes.label: Live SQL Preview Panel (S10)
nodes.rationale: Always-visible preview panel instead of Swift's toolbar link → sheet; null-safe via generateSQL(doc)?.display ?? '—'; copy-to-clipboard on the preview is in scope (S10).

nodes.label: Light-Only Decision (S1)
nodes.rationale: No dark-mode refine before SP-4a; matches creative brief Known Gaps and parent §10 (S1).

nodes.label: Swift File-Boundary Mirror Approach (S4)
nodes.rationale: One Swift view ≈ one TS module; favours port fidelity over idiomatic React structure (S4).

nodes.label: Scheduled Tech Debt (S5, §9)
nodes.rationale: React regroup deferred: port fidelity is the dominant SP-4a risk and regrouping mid-port increases the chance of silent behavior drift; paid explicitly after a green exit or when SP-4b touches the same modules, not silently (S5, §9).

nodes.label: Scaffold Purge Exit Criterion (S7)
nodes.rationale: Any leftover Tauri-React demo UI fails the exit; treated as a hard gate with grep gates for 'Welcome to Tauri', 'greet-input', 'You've been greeted', and demo logo usage (S7, §11.1).

nodes.label: No Run Button in SP-4a (S9)
nodes.rationale: Brief toolbar molecule's Primary Run is deferred to SP-4b; validation help surfaces via a status strip instead (S9).

nodes.label: CREATE Stays in SP-4a (S8)
nodes.rationale: Statement picker + CREATE root card are in scope and in exit criteria; UPDATE/DELETE remain selectable as Coming soon (S8).

nodes.label: Brief CSS Tokens on :root
nodes.rationale: Plain CSS custom properties named after brief tokens on :root; oklch() values verbatim from creative-brief.md; --radius: 4px; focus rings via outline + outline-offset; local @font-face Inter + JetBrains Mono, no CDN (§5.4).

nodes.label: Status Strip Validation Surface
nodes.rationale: Replaces Swift's toolbar runHelpMessage next to Run: shows canRun(doc, isConnected).helpMessage when not runnable (§5.2).

nodes.label: Mock Fixtures
nodes.rationale: Minimum named fixture set: default happy path (public table + non-public schema table), empty tables, empty columns, columns error — so FROM display of schema-qualified names is exercisable (§7).

nodes.label: Manual Verification Checklist (§11.2)
nodes.rationale: Manual engine verification on macOS + Linux required before SP-4a exit; Windows optional; CI stays bun run check on ubuntu-latest only (S6).

nodes.label: Direct Connection (No Server Proxy)
nodes.rationale: Design intent: the client connects directly to the user's databases so connection details, queries, and results never pass through a DragonDB server — preserving data locality and user privacy.
